claims.statement: When looking directly in a mirror the observer’s own moving eyes supply the visual input used to try to see that movement.

evidence.locator: Mirror demonstration interpreted with rapid image motion described by Wurtz.
evidence.notes: Optical/observational reasoning; mirror reflection is continuous, not frozen. Explicit optical/temporal inference using inspected mechanism; not represented as an experiment reported in the source.

caveats: Optical/observational reasoning; mirror reflection is continuous, not frozen.

claims.statement: Visual sensitivity to some stimuli is reduced around saccades; reduction is selective, not a complete interruption of all visual processing.

evidence.locator: Abstract and discussion: real versus simulated motion, time course and stimulus dependence.

claims.statement: Clear visual stimulation before and after saccades can mask awareness of the brief retinal blur during them.

evidence.locator: Suppression by visual masking, Behavioral evidence: Matin1972, Campbell/Wurtz1978 and Castet/Masson.
evidence.notes: Can mask; relative contribution depends on viewing conditions. No literal replacement frames or time deletion. Actual source body inspected.

caveats: Can mask; relative contribution depends on viewing conditions. No literal replacement frames or time deletion.

claims.statement: Watching a recording afterward separates filmed eye movement from the observer’s original saccade, permitting the movement to be inspected without making that same eye turn at the same time.

evidence.locator: Mirror phenomenon plus ordinary asynchronous camera observation; explicit inference, not a tested protocol in this study.
evidence.notes: Use later playback and steady gaze; camera frame rate/exposure can affect recording; not equivalent to direct mirror viewing. Explicit optical/temporal inference using inspected mechanism; not represented as an experiment reported in the source.

caveats: Use later playback and steady gaze; camera frame rate/exposure can affect recording; not equivalent to direct mirror viewing.
